Technical_Definition_and_Analytical_Role: Unique system-generated primary key for each individual offense entry in the database (467,601 unique values; 40,505 exact duplicates removed during cleaning).
Internal Montgomery County statutory/local offense classification code (360 unique codes) mapping to specific state or county criminal violations.
Case Report Number (467,534 unique values). Groups offenses belonging to the same police investigation/incident report.

Timestamp when Emergency Communications (911/CAD) assigned and notified a police unit to respond. Missing in 14.45% of records (73,405 rows) where reports were filed via walk-in, phone, or online without unit dispatch.
Reported or estimated date and time when the criminal offense began (supplied by the reporting party). Complete (0% missing) and serves as the primary temporal anchor.
Reported or estimated date and time when the offense concluded (e.g., the end of an overnight window when a vehicle was parked). Null in 55.59% of rows for instantaneous offenses.
Standardized federal FBI National Incident-Based Reporting System offense code (54 unique categories, e.g., 13B for Simple Assault, 23F for Theft from Motor Vehicle).
Count of individual victims associated with that specific offense row (ranges from 1 to 10 in this dataset).
Highest-level NIBRS crime taxonomy (4 values: Crime Against Person, Crime Against Property, Crime Against Society, and Not a Crime / Other).
Intermediate NIBRS offense group (54 categories, e.g., Simple Assault, All Other Larceny, Drug/Narcotic Violations), matching NIBRS Code 1-to-1.
Granular local offense description (360 descriptions, e.g., ASSAULT - 2ND DEGREE, LARCENY - FROM AUTO), matching Offence Code 1-to-1.
Name of the Montgomery County police district where the offense occurred (8 values, e.g., SILVER SPRING, WHEATON, GERMANTOWN, BETHESDA, ROCKVILLE, MONTGOMERY VILLAGE).

Privacy-redacted street address rounded to the hundred-block level (e.g., 1000 BLK MILESTONE DR). Null (7.83%) for sensitive offenses (e.g., domestic violence, sexual offenses) to protect victim privacy.
Postal city or unincorporated community name (314 raw values due to casing/spelling variations).
Two-letter US state abbreviation (MD for Maryland; 12 raw unique values reflect minor out-of-state or clerical entry noise).
5-digit US Postal Service ZIP code (206 unique values; stored as float due to 0.68% missing values).

Originating law enforcement agency (8 agencies, led by MCPD [Montgomery County Police Dept], alongside municipal departments RCPD [Rockville], GPD [Gaithersburg], TPPD [Takoma Park], and MCSO [Sheriff's Office]).
Physical premise or location type where the crime occurred (100 categories, e.g., Residence - Single Family, Street - Commercial, Parking Lot - Commercial, Retail - Mall).
Sub-district patrol sector letter code (16 values, e.g., I, N, P) used for tactical patrol deployment.
Granular patrol beat identifier (60 values, e.g., 3I1, 5N1) combining district number, sector letter, and beat number.
Police Reporting Area (808 micro-geographic zones) used by MCPD for fine-grained crime mapping and resource allocation.
Parsed hundred-block numeric component of the address (e.g., 1000.0).
Pre-directional compass indicator (N, S, E, W); 95.56% null because most streets do not carry directional prefixes.
Parsed core name of the street (8,156 unique street names, e.g., MILESTONE, GEORGIA).
Post-directional compass indicator (6 values); 98.64% null.
Standardized street thoroughfare abbreviation (35 types, e.g., RD, AVE, DR, BLV, PIKE).
WGS84 geographic latitude coordinate. Contains 0.0 (24,648 rows / 4.85% of records) when geocoding was suppressed or unavailable.
WGS84 geographic longitude coordinate. Contains 0.0 (24,648 rows / 4.85% of records) for un-geocoded entries.
Short alphanumeric code corresponding to the police district (8 values, e.g., 1D through 6D, TPPD).
Combined coordinate tuple formatted as '(Latitude, Longitude)' (e.g., '(39.0457, -76.992)'), redundant with columns 27 and 28.
